mechanism_inventory: access-control mismatch — whitelisted-filler check occurs AFTER trade execution (post-trade guard ordering flaw)
wrong lifecycle ordering — `_predyPool.trade()` is called before `msg.sender != whitelistFiller` is verified, allowing unprivileged callers to open positions if `tradeResult.minMargin > 0`
missing invariant enforcement — `gammaOrder.positionId` ownership is not verified before being passed to `_predyPool.trade()` for existing positions, allowing position hijacking
stale accounting snapshot — `userPosition.owner` in `_getOrInitPosition` checks trader after trade is already executed, so a trader field mismatch is caught too late
external-call failure / DoS — `_verifyOrder` calls `_permit2.permitWitnessTransferFrom` which could revert if permit nonce replayed or expired, blocking legitimate orders
value exceeds a logical / economic bound — `gammaOrder.leverage` is set without range validation on `userPosition.leverage`, potentially enabling positions with extreme leverage ratios

selected_mechanisms.root_cause: In `_executeTrade`, the check `if (msg.sender != whitelistFiller) { revert CallerIsNotFiller(); }` is guarded by `if (tradeResult.minMargin > 0)`, but this guard is evaluated AFTER `_predyPool.trade()` has already been called and executed. An unprivileged caller can initiate a new position (positionId == 0) and the trade executes fully before the filler check is reached. If `tradeResult.minMargin == 0` (position is closed/zeroed in one step), the filler check is bypassed entirely, allowing any caller to open and immediately close a position without being a whitelisted filler.
selected_mechanisms.attacker_model: Any unprivileged EOA can call a public function that internally calls `_executeTrade` (e.g., via the public trade entry point). By crafting a gammaOrder that results in `tradeResult.minMargin == 0` (closed position), the filler whitelist check at line 336-338 is bypassed. The trade executes with attacker-controlled parameters.
selected_mechanisms.exploit_path: 1. Attacker constructs a GammaOrder with positionId=0 (new position) and quantity/quantitySqrt values that immediately result in a closed/zero-margin position. 2. Attacker signs it and calls the public entry point. 3. `_executeTrade` is invoked: `_verifyOrder` validates the permit2 signature. 4. `_predyPool.trade()` executes the trade. 5. If `tradeResult.minMargin == 0`, the filler check at line 336 is skipped. 6. The position state is written via `_getOrInitPosition` and `_saveUserPosition`.
selected_mechanisms.who_loses: Protocol integrity — positions can be opened/closed by non-whitelisted callers, bypassing the intended gating mechanism. Traders may have positions opened or parameters set without filler oversight.
selected_mechanisms.who_gains: Attacker gains the ability to bypass the whitelisted filler requirement, potentially front-running legitimate fillers or manipulating position state.
selected_mechanisms.why_carried: Post-trade filler check ordering is a classical wrong lifecycle ordering bug. The trade executes before authorization is confirmed. The `minMargin == 0` branch is a complete bypass path. This is source-evidenced at lines 334-338.

unresolved_mechanisms.mechanism: Position ownership hijacking via crafted positionId in _executeTrade before _getOrInitPosition owner check
unresolved_mechanisms.source_evidence: In `_executeTrade` at line 319-332, `_predyPool.trade()` is called with `gammaOrder.positionId` before `_getOrInitPosition` verifies `userPosition.owner != trader` (line 581). For existing positions (positionId != 0), the trade is executed first, then the owner check fires. If the owner check reverts, the trade was already executed in `_predyPool`.
unresolved_mechanisms.unresolved_question: Whether `_predyPool.trade()` atomically rolls back on revert of subsequent operations, or whether the pre-callback state from `_predyPool.trade()` persists even if this contract reverts after. If the predyPool trade is committed before the revert in this contract, an attacker can execute trades on a vault they don't own then trigger a revert to preserve some benefit.
unresolved_mechanisms.who_loses: Position owner — their vault/position may have been traded against before the revert.
unresolved_mechanisms.who_gains: Attacker — may be able to move prices or extract value during the trade window.

unresolved_mechanisms.mechanism: Missing leverage bounds validation on userPosition.leverage assignment
unresolved_mechanisms.source_evidence: At line 347, `userPosition.leverage = gammaOrder.leverage` is assigned directly from the order without any range check or maximum bound enforcement visible in the source.
unresolved_mechanisms.unresolved_question: Whether `leverage` is validated inside `_saveUserPosition` / `GammaTradeMarketLib.saveUserPosition`, which is not present in the provided source. If no validation occurs, an attacker could set extreme leverage values affecting downstream delta calculations and liquidation thresholds.
unresolved_mechanisms.who_loses: Protocol liquidity providers and counterparties if extreme leverage causes under-collateralization.
unresolved_mechanisms.who_gains: Attacker gains a position with unusually high leverage beyond intended risk parameters.

rejected_mechanisms.mechanism: External-call failure / DoS via permit2 nonce replay blocking legitimate orders
rejected_mechanisms.rejecting_source_fact: Permit2 nonce replay and expiration are standard EIP-712 / Permit2 protections. A replayed or expired signature causes the caller's OWN transaction to revert, not other users' orders. Each user has their own nonce space. The revert does not affect other orders or lock the contract.
rejected_mechanisms.why_unexploitable: An attacker cannot cause another user's order to fail by replaying their own permit; each permit is user-specific. No griefing vector exists here beyond normal permit expiry.
rejected_mechanisms.who_loses: The submitter of the replayed/expired permit (themselves).

impact_direction.attacker_receives: Ability to bypass the whitelisted-filler gate and execute trades on the GammaTradeMarket without authorization, potentially front-running legitimate fillers or forcing unauthorized position state changes.
impact_direction.attacker_preserves: Attacker's funds are not spent — the permit2 transfer goes to the contract but the position is opened under the trader's (victim's) identity per the signed order.
impact_direction.victim_loses: Protocol invariant that only whitelisted fillers can open new positions is violated; the gating mechanism designed to prevent unauthorized position creation is bypassable when minMargin equals zero.
impact_direction.invariant_violated: Whitelisted-filler-only invariant for opening positions: 'only whitelisted filler can open position' comment at line 335 is bypassed when the trade results in minMargin == 0.
impact_direction.not_self_funded_or_dust_or_admin_or_timi: The bypass is permissionless (no special role required), affects real position state on-chain, and is not dust or timing-dependent — it depends on crafting an order that results in a zero minMargin outcome.

stop_condition: more_mechanisms_pending: Two unresolved mechanisms remain in unresolved_mechanisms — position-hijacking atomicity (NEEDS_HARNESS) and leverage bounds validation (NEEDS_HARNESS). These affect different state variables (vaultId ownership and leverage) from the primary filler-bypass mechanism, and the leverage mechanism could affect protocol solvency at a potentially higher severity tier.
